To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the time operation mode of scintillation detectors for measuring the induced activity 12B and N at the pulsed accelerator can be used to measure the induced activity of 12N and B in objects of study at pulsed electron accelerators.

the use of a scintillation detector with a photoelectron multiplier divider in a switching mode makes it possible to measure the induced activity of 12N (and also 12B) at pulsed electron accelerators.
it is possible to use scintillation detectors with photoelectron multiplier divisors to measure the induced activity of 12N and12B in time intervals between beam pulses of an accelerator.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of the method and the design of an experimental facility for measuring the induced activity at pulsed electron accelerators.
the development of the time operation mode of the detectors for measuring the induced activity in the objects of study at pulsed electron accelerators.
the development of the time operation mode of scintillation detectors in order to increase their efficiency in detecting short-lived radioisotope particles.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the method proposed is effective for detecting and measuring the induced activity in objects of study at the decay of 12N and12B, which have short half-lives.

, in order to measure the induced activity of 12N and/or 12B, the time operation mode of the scintillation detector should be switched to the "on" state during the time intervals between beam pulses, i.e., when the object is irradiated with beam pulses, the scintillation detection system is switched to the "off" state, and, after the end of irradiation, the scintillations detection system is switched back to the "on state.

this method of switching on and off the photoelectron multiplier divisors on the scintillator detectors allows one to obtain the time profile of the induced activities of 12B, 12N and their daughter nuclei in the object of study.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the switching method for scintillation detectors is effective and allows one to increase the sensitivity of the detectors for measuring the induced activities of short-lived radio-isotopes by 1.5–2 times.

, for the given time intervals between the pulses and for the given beam current, the time operation modes of the scintillation detector for measuring 12B and the induced activity of 12N are the same.

the switching method for power supplies of the photoelectron multipliers is an effective way to increase the efficiency of the detection of the decay products of 12N and of 12B in the time intervals between pulses of a pulsed electron beam.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the time operation mode of the scintillation detector is a key parameter for the efficiency of measuring the induced 12N and induced 12B activities.

the time interval between the beam pulse and the switching of the photoelectron multiplier divider power supply on the scintillators used to detect the particles emitted from the irradiated objects at the decay 12N and12B must be no less than the decay half-lives of 12N and of 12B.

the switching method is effective for measuring the induced activity in objects with short-lived radioisotope products when the beam pulse repetition time is 100 ms or more and the beam power is up to 1 kW.
